"We just need a vote."
That's the problem in five words.
22 million Americans' healthcare affordability depends on:
→ Whether Congress schedules a vote
→ Whether it passes
→ Whether it survives the next Congress
→ Whether the next administration enforces it

Healthcare costs shouldn't be this politically fragile.
What one Congress gives, another takes. What one bill fixes, another unfixes. Every election cycle, millions become bargaining chips.

The alternative: coverage structures that don't depend on votes. Member-owned pools where the rules are set by members, not legislators. Transparency by architecture, not mandate.

Good luck with the bill @RepGregLandsman Genuinely. But we're also building systems that don't need congressional permission:

@apollocareio  blockchain-based, member-governed health coverage. Because 22 million people shouldn't hold their breath waiting for a vote.
